## Function Build Retry

The retry card <base>.r<n> carrying the acceptance output and the previous attempt diff; at most 2 retries per card; a run-wide cap on retry batches is enforced by Run Deck.

Behaviour: buildRetry(card, attempt, acceptanceOutput, previousDiff) returns a NEW Card. attempt must be 1 or 2, else it throws Error "buildRetry: attempt must be 1 or 2". ## Function Process Generation

compile → send → parse → verify per card; a compile fault or stale inputs discard the answer; accepted cards fire the commit hook.

Behaviour: processGeneration(cards, deps, root) compiles every card with compileCard, keeping each card's input digest; sends all variants of all cards in ONE sendGeneration(deps.config, requests, deps.transport) call (so deps.config's concurrency pools across the whole generation) and slices answers and usage back to each card by request index; then verifies each card in input order. Per card: a compile fault → {status: "failed", reason "compile: <first fault message>", acceptanceLog = the fault messages joined by "\n"}; else recompute the digest (captureInputs) and compareCaptures against the compile digest — a non-empty change → {status: "failed", reason "stale inputs", acceptanceLog "stale inputs: <changed paths, comma+space joined>"} and no acceptance is run; else build one VariantAnswer per variant (variant id "<customId>.v<n>"; a null-text answer becomes {corrupt: the answer's error ?? "no text returned"}, else parseAnswer(text, targets)) and call verifyCard. Accepted → {status: "written", winningVariant = the accepted variant id, acceptanceLog = the winner's log, earlierFailures = the logs of the rejected variants tried before it, commit = the sha from deps.commit(customId, targets), diffstat from the hook}; no variant accepted → {status: "failed", reason "acceptance failed", acceptanceLog = the last variant's log, earlierFailures = the earlier variants' logs, commit null, diffstat null}. attempts is 1 for every outcome of one round. Returns {outcomes, usage, requests, retryContexts}: usage is the Usage of every request sent; requests is one Request Usage per request sent, in send order ({customId: the request id, model: the request's model ?? deps.config.model, provider, generationId, inputTokens, outputTokens, cost from its Usage, finishReason and error from its Answer}); retryContexts holds one Retry Context per FAILED outcome, keyed by its customId, in outcome order, and nothing for a written card. A compile fault or stale inputs → {acceptanceOutput: the outcome's acceptanceLog, previousDiff: null}. A rejected card → the LAST variant whose acceptance ran (its verify result has a diff that is not null) gives {acceptanceOutput: that variant's log, previousDiff: its diff, or null when the diff is ""}; when no variant ran (every answer corrupt or truncated) → {acceptanceOutput: the last result's log, previousDiff: null}. The log and the diff of the retry always come from the same attempt.

## Function Run Deck

Generations in order (layerGenerations), budget checked at each generation boundary (maxCards, maxRetryBatches, deadline), the Run Report produced at the end.

Behaviour: runDeck(input, deps) runs input.deck generation by generation in the order of layerGenerations(input.deck). At each generation boundary it checks the budget: deps.now() >= input.budget.deadline → every not-yet-done card of this and the later generations becomes {status: "budget-exceeded", reason "deadline"}; cardsProcessed >= input.budget.maxCards → reason "maxCards <maxCards>". Otherwise it resolves the runnable cards (resolveRunnable with the statuses so far), records the skipped outcomes, runs processGeneration on the runnable cards, accumulates their usage and request rows, keeps the Retry Context of every failed card (by its original id; a later round's context replaces an earlier one), and adds the runnable count to cardsProcessed. A card that failed is retried: for the failed cards of a round, while retryBatches < input.budget.maxRetryBatches and the card has been retried fewer than 2 times, a retry batch runs (retryBatches += 1): buildRetry(original card, retryNumber, the card's latest Retry Context acceptanceOutput, its previousDiff) for each — so the retry carries the output and the diff of the same failed attempt — processGeneration on the retries, and a retry that is written updates the card's outcome (status "written", its commit, attempts = the retry number + 1) while every attempt's log is appended to earlierFailures. At the end it builds the Run Report: runId, completedAt = deps.now(), branch = input.branch, processor = deps.config.id, generations = the generation count, outcomes in deck order, usageTotals {inputTokens, outputTokens summed; cost the sum of the reported costs or null when none was reported; requests = the number of usage rows}, requests = every Request Usage row of every processGeneration call of the run, in send order. Returns {report, outcomes}. It writes and commits nothing: the archive is P6 git's.

Steps:

Data Run Report: The summary of one run (its schema and archive layout are runloop's; the file write and commit are P6 git's).

{ runId: string, completedAt: number, branch: string, processor: string, generations: number, outcomes: CardOutcome[], usageTotals: { inputTokens: number, outputTokens: number, cost: number | null, requests: number }, requests?: RequestUsage[] } — requests is always set by Run Deck; it is optional in the type so a report literal built elsewhere stays valid

## Component requirements / guardrails

Requirements:
- Strict TypeScript: tsconfig strict, ESM, no `any`; every module compiles with tsc --noEmit.
- One Document Out: Every command prints exactly one JSON document on stdout and nothing else; the human log goes to stderr.
- Deterministic Core: cards and compiler give byte-identical results for the same inputs: no clock, no randomness, no environment reads. acceptance is bound only in its pure parts (Snapshot Targets, Build Attempt Diff): Run Acceptance spawns a shell and its only timer is the child's timeout; env and the timeout are parameters, never process.env (06.10, P3). processor reads the environment only in Read Registry; Assemble Request, Read Response and Stub Answer are pure of clock and network; the transport and its sleep are parameters of Send Generation (P4). git spawns only in Run Git, synchronously, with the child's environment given whole as a parameter; it reads no process.env and no clock of its own (P6). cli touches the process only in its entry src/cli.ts: the environment, the working directory, the clock and the output streams reach main() as parameters, and the environment reaches the processor only through Read Registry (P7). language is pure data and pure functions: no clock, no environment, no file system, no child process; node:path is its only Node module; its shell lines are text (P8). contour reads no file, no clock and no environment: it parses the text it is given; the package yaml is imported in Parse Document alone (P9).
- Node Only: Runtime dependencies: Node 20 built-ins and the package `yaml` (the record reader), nothing else; dev dependencies pinned exactly, no ^ or ~.

Guardrails:
- No Network In Tests: tests/setup.ts makes fetch, XMLHttpRequest, WebSocket and net.connect throw "network blocked in tests"; only the processor's own transport is mocked.
- No Shell Outside Acceptance: child processes are spawned only by Run Acceptance, the git module (in Run Git alone, P6) and the processor's none; everything else is pure.
- Frozen Tree During Run: while a run is in flight no file outside the cards' targets and .morph/ changes; a changed declared input discards the answer unread.
